title: WORK-LAB local model registry — physical model assets and their capability declarations
purpose: Single machine-readable truth for which local model weights exist, what they are, where they physically live, and which capability each one serves. Business code must reference a logical provider id from provider-registry.json, never a file path, a quant name or an absolute Windows path.
precedence: WORK-LAB-AUTHORITY.md > .project/governance/project-authority-index.json > this file. This file records the model control plane; it does not grant execution authority.

benchmark.thinking_mode: must set chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking:false}; otherwise the token budget is consumed by reasoning and the visible answer is empty
benchmark.sample_answer_zh: 1. 降低存储成本与硬件压力… 2. 简化版本管理与一致性… 3. 提升部署与更新效率…
benchmark.bandwidth_bound: 13.27 GB at ~38 GB/s DDR4-3600 caps a dense 27B near 2.7 tok/s; the measured 2.52 is ~93% of that ceiling

models.serving_note: With the desktop's GPU footprint released (VRAM used 6.8 -> 2.0 GiB) offload finally pays: ngl 0 -> 32 lifted generation 1.32 -> 2.52 tok/s (+91%) and prompt 14.54 -> 20.10 (+38%), then went flat from ngl 16 to 32 because only about a third of the model fits in 8 GiB. The dense 27B is memory-bandwidth bound on DDR4-3600, so it is usable for batch/long-form work but slow for interactive chat. For interactive 30B-class work the already-installed qwen3-coder:30b-a3b MoE measured 7.81 tok/s (3.9x faster) — recorded as a data point, not a substitution, since the brief fixes DEEP = Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ4_XS.

models.vision_defect: The GGUF was parsed directly: arch=qwen25vl but hasVision=false — there is no clip.* key and no mmproj file anywhere in the shared library, and the Ollama manifest carries a single image.model layer. The blob is therefore a text-only 7B and cannot do OCR under any runtime.

replacement.why: the llama.cpp project's own repository ships a matched vision projector

No 64-hex digest is claimed because no earlier record carries a prefix to identify these files against — asserting one would be a digest with no provenance.
